newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: SABIC sees lower 1996 net profits.
newsitem.headline: SABIC sees lower 1996 net profits.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial heavyweight Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) has predicted lower net profits for full-year 1996 despite an increase in production and sales.
"SABIC production and sales were up in 1996, profits will be less than 1995's record earnings," SABIC's chairman Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani said in a statement.

"The profit decline was caused primarily by depressed product prices that reflected the highly competitive chemical industry environment worldwide," said Yamani, who is also Saudi Arabia's industry and electricity minister. He gave no figures for 1996.
SABIC, 70 percent owned by the Saudi government, posted a record 6.28 billion riyals ($1.67 billion) profit in 1995, up from 4.20 billion riyals in 1994.
SABIC, which accounts for five percent of total world production of petrochemicals, sold 15 tonnes in the first 10 months of 1996, up seven percent from 1995, Yamani said.

"Despite higher rates of overall performance, profit gains were lessened due to lower world prices for many of SABIC's chemical products, especially polyethylene, polyvinyl chloride, styrene, ethylene glycol and methanol," Yamani said.
